questions.prompt: Choose two checks before using low support.

options.text: The assumption that a covered slot must still be forced
Whether the low route remains open
Whether F1 can receive away from Gold 2

questions.explanation: Low support may preserve possession, but it creates another read rather than a guaranteed scoring chance.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possession reset decision.

options.text: Recognize the crowded slot route
Compare low and high outlets
Use an available connection and reoffer

questions.explanation: Recognizing the crowded slot and comparing low/high outlets can overlap, since scanning continues the whole time; the routine only fixes that using a connection and reoffering come last, because the actual pass or carry cannot happen before that read. A shot or carry remains possible if the picture changes; this routine does not ban them.

questions.prompt: Move YOU off the puck-side half wall to compare a new low-support angle.
questions.explanation: The example changes the relation to Gold 1 and F1. Other pockets may preserve possession better under live pressure.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 leaves the slot route to pressure YOU on the wall. What should be checked?

options.text: Only the low pass from the old picture
Whether F2’s route has become usable
The assumption that the slot is still covered identically

questions.explanation: A defender leaving one responsibility can open another, but Gold 2 may still affect the pass.

questions.prompt: Name two support areas in this scene and explain the different choices they offer.
questions.explanation: Contrast below the goal line with the high point or slot. Describe the pressure, not merely the geography.

questions.prompt: Which pressure call matches the current direct passing lines from YOU?

options.text: Gold 1 is nearer the line to F2 than the line to F1; compare the low outlet

questions.explanation: Gold 1 is close to the direct slot line toward F2. The low line to F1 passes farther away from Gold 1, but Gold 2 and the receiving space still need checking.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect low support?

options.text: Gold 1 leaves the slot route
F2 remains a reachable outlet

questions.explanation: Slot pressure and outlet access shape the low-support decision.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the goal line to compare an exchange angle near F1.
questions.explanation: The example brings the carrier nearer F1. Check Gold 1 and Gold 2 before using that exchange; possession is still with YOU.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 pressures YOU on the wall. What should be checked?
questions.explanation: Check F1, the slot lane and F2 before choosing protection, pass, or a reset; the wall pressure changes the original angle.
